title: Amendment of the fines relating to offences under the Employment of Women, Young Persons and Children Act, No.47 of 1956
decision_details: - The Employment of Women, Young Persons and Children Act, No.47 of 1956, completely prohibits the employment of children below the age of 16 years and in accordance with the provisions of the said Act, regulations have been imposed to be followed by employers regarding the employment of young persons above the age of 16 but below the age of 18. According to the relevant Act and the regulations issued in accordance with the provisions of the said Act, it is a punishable offence to employ children and young persons of the relevant age group in hazardous occupation that may be detrimental to health, safety and morals. The Amendment made to the said Act in the year 2003 has introduced provisions to impose a fine not exceeding Rs.10,000/- or imprisonment for a period not exceeding 12 months or both such fine and imprisonment and also to order compensation to the prejudicated child at the discretion of the Court, on a person found guilty under the provision of the said Act. However, it has been observed that the amount of the relevant fine is inadequate. Therefore, the proposal made by the Minister of Labour to update and revise the minimum fines mentioned in sections 7(3), 13(2) and 20(a)(3) of the Employment of Women, Young Persons and Children Act, No.47, 1956, complying with the Convention No. 138 and 182 of the International Labour Organization which have been ratified by Sri Lanka, was approved by the Cabinet.
